newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy treasury to up ENI share offer to public.
newsitem.headline: Italy treasury to up ENI share offer to public.

text.p: The Italian Treasury said on Wednesday that it would substantially increase the amount of shares of energy giant ENI being offered to the Italian public in the face of heavy demand.
A statement also said the Treasury would examine the global scale of the offer with a view to a possible increase in the overall number of shares it will make available to various investors.

"In relation to this increase (to private Italian investors), the Treasury Ministry will examine as soon possible the opportunity of increasing the amount originally provided for the global offer," the statement said.
Of the total 700 million of shares, some 300 million are being offered to Italian retail investors, 235 million to institutional investors and 165 million to investors in the United States.

Global coordinators for the sale, Italian investment bank IMI and CS First Boston, have been granted an over-allotment or "green-shoe" option of a further 105 million shares which will be offered to institutional investors in the case of heavy demand.
The Treasury has said previously that the offer, which accounts for 8.75 percent of ENI's share capital, or 10 percent if the green shoe is included, could be increased if demand was strong enough.
In November 1995, the Treasury sold a first 15 percent tranche of ENI shares at 5,250 lire a share to trade in Milan London and New York, which raised 6.3 trillion lire.
ENI shares closed on the Milan bourse on Wednesday at 7,402 lire, down 58.
Public subscription to the offer in Italy runs from October 21 to 25 and the final share price will be fixed on October 26 with trading is expected to start on October 28.
The statement said demand was double the amount on offer to the public after only three days.
The Treasury has said the public offer will be priced at either 7,425 lire or at Friday's closing price less a 3.5 percent discount, whichever is lower.
